title: Which Samsung Galaxy phones are nearing the end of life - Sammy Fans
text:
Samsung is still supporting Galaxy devices released way back in 2021. Those models landed with a software guarantee of five years. However, newer Galaxy phones and tablets support even longer updates, up to seven years. 

If you get a Samsung device launched in August 2026, it will receive software updates until August 2033. This is a massive seven years of software support the Korean tech giant is presently offering on its flagship Galaxy lineup. Even if you get a mid-range or budget model, you are covered for up to six years of updates. 

What makes Samsung updates impressive is the rollout frequency. Premium Galaxy phones and select mid-range models get new updates every month. Other phones and all tablets (as well as watches) get a new update every quarter. 

That said, flagship Samsung phones released in 2021 and others in 2022 are nearing the end of life. Android updates stop a year prior to security patches, as Samsung keeps letting users rock with their devices for an additional year. 

#### What Samsung Galaxy phones are nearing the end of life

Note that the list is not final, nor provided by Samsung. This is compiled based on the software support data publicly available. Device(s) could still get new software updates after hitting the end of life defined by Samsung.

title: Galaxy A54/A34 Update Policy: Android 17 and 2028 Support
text:
Samsung’s long-support promise for the Galaxy A54 5G and A34 5G is real, but the headline needs updating: both phones are on Android 16, Android 17 should be final, and security support should last roughly into 2028.

...

Yes, Samsung’s unusually long support promise for the Galaxy A54 5G and Galaxy A34 5G is real. Both phones launched with Android 13 and were promised four Android OS upgrades plus five years of security updates. As of August 10, 2026, both have reached Android 16, so Android 17 should be the final major Android upgrade. Security support should continue roughly into 2028, although the exact schedule depends on the model, country, carrier, and variant.

The important update to the original 2023 claim is that this is no longer a prediction about future support. The phones have already received Android 14, Android 15, and Android 16. They still have meaningful support remaining, but buyers should evaluate them based on the remaining window rather than the original five-year headline.

...

In its launch announcement, Samsung said the Galaxy A54 5G and Galaxy A34 5G would receive four Android OS updates and five years of security updates. Samsung used qualifying language such as up to, so the promise should not be interpreted as a guarantee that every country, carrier, or model variant will receive each release on the same day or with exactly the same features.

...

Both phones launched in March 2023 with Android 13 and One UI 5.1. On that starting point, four major Android upgrades means:

- Android 14
- Android 15
- Android 16
- Android 17

That is a stronger policy than many mid-range phones received when these models launched. Samsung’s official launch announcement is the source of the commitment; it is not merely an interpretation made by third-party coverage.

...

## Android 17 should be the final major upgrade

Because the A54 5G and A34 5G started on Android 13 and Samsung promised four Android OS upgrades, Android 17 should be the final major Android version for both phones. That is the logical result of Samsung’s policy, not confirmation that Android 17 has already arrived on these devices.

The official firmware records reviewed on August 10, 2026 still identify both models as running Android 16. Samsung’s current One UI 9 announcement says One UI 9 is based on Android 17, but that announcement concerns the Galaxy S26 beta program and does not provide a model-specific final-release schedule for the A54 5G or A34 5G. The most accurate wording is therefore expected Android 17 support, probably delivered as One UI 9, rather than a claim that either phone is already running it.

### The four-upgrade timeline

| Stage | Underlying Android version | Samsung interface | How it counts |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Launch, March 2023 | Android 13 | One UI 5.1 | Starting version |
| First major upgrade | Android 14 | One UI 6 | Upgrade one of four |
| Second major upgrade | Android 15 | One UI 7 | Upgrade two of four |
| Third major upgrade | Android 16 | One UI 8 | Upgrade three of four |
| Intermediate feature release | Android 16 | One UI 8.5 | Not a new Android generation |
| Expected final major upgrade | Android 17 | Likely One UI 9 | Upgrade four of four |

One UI and Android are related but different labels. Android is the underlying operating-system generation. One UI is Samsung’s interface and feature layer. The security patch level identifies the date of the security fixes included in a package, while the build number identifies the exact firmware package. Confusing these labels can make a normal interface update look like an extra Android upgrade.

## Current firmware status as of August 10, 2026

Samsung’s official firmware records show that both phones are still receiving software. The entries below are useful, verifiable examples—not universal release dates for every A54 or A34.

### Galaxy A54 5G: U.S. example

For model SM-A546U, Samsung’s firmware record shows:

- Build: A546USQSLFZG3
- Release date: July 30, 2026
- Android version: Android 16
- Security patch level: July 5, 2026

The same record lists an earlier One UI 8.5 build, A546USQUJFZEA, released June 9, 2026 with the May 5, 2026 security patch. This is a U.S. model record; the update available to a particular owner can differ by carrier, CSC, and distribution wave. See Samsung’s SM-A546U firmware history.

### Galaxy A34 5G: international/EU example

For model SM-A346B, Samsung’s record shows:

- Build: A346BXXSGFZG4
- Release date: August 3, 2026
- Android version: Android 16
- Security patch level: July 5, 2026

The A34 record also lists One UI 8.5 build A346BXXUFFZE6, released June 8, 2026 with the May 5, 2026 security patch. This is an international/EU example and should not be treated as the schedule for U.S. or other regional models. See Samsung’s SM-A346B firmware history.

...

Samsung’s international SM-A546B record shows Android 16 and One UI 8.5, including a June 29, 2026 build carrying the June 5, 2026 security patch. The A34’s South Korean SM-A3460 record shows Android 16 and One UI 8.5 with a June 11, 2026 release date. These records demonstrate active support, but also demonstrate why a firmware date for one variant cannot be applied to every phone sold under the same retail name.

...

## One UI 8.5 is not a fifth Android update

One UI 8.5 is a Samsung interface and feature release built on Android 16 for these phones. It does not reset or extend the four-generation Android count.

This distinction matters when reading an update screen:

- Android version: the major Google operating-system generation, such as Android 16.
- One UI version: Samsung’s software layer, such as One UI 8 or One UI 8.5.
- Security patch level: the date of the security fixes included in the installed build.
- Build number: the precise firmware package installed on the device.

Samsung’s Hong Kong One UI 8.5 schedule listed the Galaxy A54 5G as completed on June 9, 2026 and the Galaxy A34 5G for July 2026 in that market. Samsung also warned that schedules could change or be temporarily paused. That schedule is market-specific and is not evidence that every country received the update on those dates. The notice is available on Samsung Hong Kong’s support page.

## How long will security support last?

Samsung’s five-year security commitment points to support lasting approximately into 2028, because both phones launched in March 2023. This is an estimated support horizon, not a publicly stated universal end date such as March 16, 2028.

There are two important limits to the headline:

1. Five years is not five years after the final Android upgrade. Android 17 should be the fourth and final major upgrade, while security maintenance continues within the overall support period.
2. Five years does not mean identical monthly delivery everywhere. Samsung varies update availability and timing by market, exact model, network provider, and carrier. A final patch may arrive at a different time—or in a different package—for different variants.

Samsung’s current security-update scope page also notes that its listed models and schedules can change. Some chipset-specific fixes may arrive in a later package rather than the same month they become available.

...

The long-term Android promise is essentially the same for both phones, but Samsung’s current published security categories differ:

| Phone | Samsung-listed cadence | What that means in practice |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Galaxy A54 5G | Monthly security-update category | The stronger listed cadence, particularly for supported enterprise or certain international variants |
| Galaxy A34 5G | Quarterly security-update category | Still officially supported, but patches are generally grouped less frequently |

Samsung lists the A54 under monthly security updates in the page’s Enterprise Models section and the A34 under quarterly updates in the Galaxy A Series section. This classification does not guarantee that every A54 will receive a patch in every calendar month or that every A34 will wait exactly three months.

...

## Release date and security patch date are different

The A34 SM-A346B build released on August 3, 2026 carries the July 5, 2026 security patch. The A54 SM-A546U build released on July 30 carries the same July 5 patch. That is normal: the date Samsung uploads or distributes a firmware build is not necessarily the date of the security fixes inside it.

When checking a phone or a used listing, record both dates where available. A recent build with an older patch level is not automatically a sign that the phone is unsupported, while a device with an old build and a very old patch level deserves closer investigation.

...

For an existing owner, the support policy remains a genuine advantage. Both phones are already on Android 16, Android 17 is still expected, and security support should continue roughly into 2028. The A54 also has the stronger currently listed security cadence.

The qualification is age. By August 2026, these are March 2023 phones. Their remaining value is concentrated in one expected major Android release and the remaining security-support period, not in several more years of major Android versions. Battery wear, storage, modem compatibility, screen condition, and repair cost may matter more than the software promise for a particular owner.

...

## Bottom line

Samsung’s 2023 support promise has largely held up. The Galaxy A54 5G and Galaxy A34 5G were promised four Android OS upgrades and five years of security updates; both are on Android 16 as of August 10, 2026; and Android 17 should be their final major Android upgrade. Security patches are expected to continue approximately into 2028, with delivery frequency and end timing dependent on the exact model, region, and carrier.

Dutch site GalaxyClub reports that firmware A546BXXUNGZJ5 is available in the Netherlands, Belgium and the rest of Europe. The rollout started in Korea on 28 October. This is the A54’s fourth and final major Android upgrade under Samsung’s promise.

So Samsung has kept its OS promise to A54 owners. Security patches should keep coming after this, though. Up to five years from the March 2023 launch points to updates running into early 2028. title: Samsung Galaxy update support up to 7 years; how long will my device be supported?
text:
[Digi

...

According to IT outlet Engadget on Oct. 11 local time, Samsung smartphones support operating system updates for up to 7 years for flagship models, 5 to 6 years for mid-range models and about 4 years at most for entry-level models.

This year, Android 17 led software changes for smartphones, focusing on productivity-enhancing features. Samsung Electronics has already applied One UI 9 based on Android 17 to the Galaxy Fold8 series and the Flip8. Unlike the latest devices, older models run security updates and operating system updates differently. Security patches are provided for a relatively long time, but operating system updates that include feature changes often end earlier.

The gap in support periods is more pronounced in the Galaxy A series. Engadget pointed out that this tendency is stronger in Samsung’s entry-level A series. In practice, the Galaxy A34 and A54 5G receive Android updates until March 2027, but the Galaxy A73 is no longer eligible from April 2026.

Some tablet models receive longer support. The Galaxy Tab Active5 supports Android updates until January 2028. The Galaxy Tab Active5 Pro will continue to be supported through 2033. Wearable devices are also still eligible for updates this year, but the original text did not specify individual model names separately.

The article also presented it as key that users must check Samsung device support themselves. Manufacturers often do not warn in advance when software or security updates end. The article said manufacturers do not separately notify users before stopping updates, and advised users to look up their smartphone model online to confirm. Samsung Electronics provides a list of devices eligible for security updates, which can be used to check current support status.

If the last update date in the Settings app has been stuck for months or years rather than days, there is a high chance support has already ended. End of support does not stop at simply missing new features. If security patches stop, the device can become more vulnerable to new hacking threats. Engadget also warned that losing security patches can expose smartphones to various new attacks.
